messages.msg: Q14 explains call order on StoryCard with two calls, likes first and isBookmarked second, and logs both values on each render. Q37 can break that same order (a useState inside if (likes > 0)) so the reader sees the rule fail on code they already know. React 19.3 then logs 'React has detected a change in the order of Hooks called by StoryCard' and throws 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render.' Recall the model from Q14 state-lives-in-react rather than teaching it again.

messages.msg: Lecture 2 teaches that our code never calls a component as a function, writes <ArticleCard /> instead of {ArticleCard()}, and notes that the hand call gives the same article for now. It promises that Lecture 37 shows the cost: once a component uses Hooks, a hand call makes its Hooks belong to the caller, so state mixes and the order of Hooks breaks. Please cite Lecture 2 when you show it.

Q14 explains how React tells state values apart on ArticleCard with two useState calls at the top, likes first and isSaved second (two Likes and a Save show Like (2) and Saved). Its real mistake already breaks the order: a useState inside if (likes > 0) makes React 19.3.1 log 'React has detected a change in the order of Hooks' and throw 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render.' on the first Like, and useState inside a handler throws 'Invalid hook call.' Q37 can recall the model from Q14 state-lives-in-react and explain why the order may never change, on the same ArticleCard, instead of teaching the model again.
